title: Repair PR 47 CI regressions
summary: Repairs PR 47 CI regressions in strict pending-publish manifests, close-readiness validation, command-journal validation, WebView focus and rendering behavior, release assertions, tooling previews, lint accounting, generated contracts, browser census evidence, and development dependency declarations.
reason: The pull request introduced stricter contracts, hardened Tauri behavior, and new WebView controls without synchronizing every manifest field, close-readiness normalizer, release assertion, dependency, generated baseline, lint budget, and browser assertion. It also allowed oversized rejected command-journal scalars to reach expensive regex redaction.
behavior_before: Strict rerun manifests and copied sidecars omitted output hash proof, malformed close-readiness could retain apparent backend authority, oversized invalid journal requests could exceed the API timeout, quick-link focus could remain on the trigger during queued refreshes, tooling preview required locally installed client CLIs, maintenance rendering assumed an array, and CI baselines and assertions did not match the new controls.
behavior_after: Strict rerun manifests and copied sidecars include SHA-256 proof, malformed or contradictory close-readiness fails closed, journal redaction receives bounded scalar text, quick-link focus claims the requested destination before preserving later user focus, tooling preview remains non-mutating without installed clients, maintenance rendering safely handles absent rows, and CI dependencies, generated contracts, lint accounting, and release assertions match the implemented behavior.
manual_validation: 158 targeted Python tests and 640 subtests passed
Command-journal timeout and policy tests passed: 19 tests and 27 subtests
Dependency boundary check passed with zero unallowlisted hard findings; 43 launch, snapshot, and priority-export tests plus 40 subtests passed
Direct ESLint verification reported no warnings for runMonitorView.js
Evidence and root control censuses passed; shell census uses an exact accepted split for timing-dependent controls
Home live-state browser smoke passed twice consecutively
Pending-publish, snapshot, topbar, and cross-page tests passed: 6 tests and 565 subtests
WebView asset syntax, generated map, DOM gap, routes, commands, script order, public contract, and touchpoint checks passed
npm run webview:prework:check passed at 1380/1387 warnings with zero errors; 107 focused WebView tests and 451 subtests passed
The complete rerun-results, close-readiness, CSS token, code-context preview, and run-monitor static modules passed: 75 tests
The Home live-state browser smoke passed twice after the focus-claim correction
Current WebView reliability checks passed, including updated Tauri bootstrap-origin and bounded-output redaction assertions
Library Route Map guided-focus browser smoke passed twice; touchpoint-ledger pytest module passed all 7 tests
Portable-package pytest-style validation passed: 33 passed and 3 expected source-only checks skipped
Home, Settings/Launch, prose-box audit, and Queue/Launch/Completed browser smokes passed together after the final guided-focus refinement
rollback_plan: Revert this change as one commit. No persisted state migration is required; pending manifests created after this change retain compatible additive hash fields.
notes:
Python impact is limited to bounding rejected command-journal scalar redaction and including existing output-hash evidence for strict pending-publish media and copied sidecars. No media policy, source mutation, route contract, or publish/drain decision changed. Representative real-media validation is not required because the pending-publish change is additive manifest evidence covered by hermetic contract tests.
PR-added process-to-queue imports were replaced by queue-service capability calls, preserving queue ownership and removing the new package-cycle edge.
Follow-up removes the clean-CI lint regressions by extracting low-complexity topbar helpers, removing dead timeline locals, moving stateless priority helpers outside the factory, and declaring the shared lastQueue binding writable.
The final CI follow-up makes close-readiness normalization fail closed, stabilizes quick-link and guided-route focus across asynchronous rerenders, keeps setup preview and source-only pytest-style checks portable, aligns release assertions with the hardened Tauri origin and output-log implementations, replaces raw CSS values with design tokens, and refreshes affected generated evidence. Full WebView prework passed locally using the isolated worktree with the configured checkout's dependency tree linked read-only for validation. Full local package verification continued past pytest-style validation and then stopped only because this local worktree did not reproduce CI's provisioned FFmpeg, ffprobe, MKVToolNix, and PgsToSrt tool payloads.
